page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.3xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz, offering 6 physical cores and 12 virtual CPUs through multi-threading. The memory configuration provides 24.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Cache specifications include 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. Advanced hardware extensions are present, including AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, SHA_NI, and VAES. Network performance features an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Local ephemeral disk storage and dedicated GPUs are absent from this instance type.

Benchmark results for the ecs.c7.3xlarge place its core computing capabilities within average expected ranges. Single-core performance yields a Geekbench score of 1531.0 and a stress-ng score of 1874.59, while multi-core testing reaches a Geekbench score of 7760.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 16209.01. Memory bandwidth is measured at 76.48 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 46.87 GB/sec for large writes. Workload-specific tests record 11.74 million Redis SET operations per second, 15.7 GB/sec static web serving throughput, and a software compilation score of 11558.0 in Geekbench. Without dedicated GPU hardware, prompt processing for 7B parameter language models falls into a weaker relative category at 23.52 tokens per second.

The ecs.c7.3xlarge provides a balanced density profile for CPU-intensive tasks that do not depend on high memory ratios or local storage. Its instruction set support suits vector operations and cryptographic tasks. Recommended workloads include software compilation, web serving, CI/CD pipelines, and database caching layers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.3xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 instance featuring a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor with 6 physical cores and 12 virtual CPUs. The instance delivers 24.0 GB of RAM, 48 MB of L3 cache, and an 8 Gbps baseline network capacity. It includes hardware acceleration support for AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and SHA_NI, while omitting local storage and dedicated GPUs. Performance benchmarks sit within average ranges, recording a PassMark CPU score of 16209.01, a Geekbench multi-core score of 7760.0, and a Redis throughput of 11.74 million SET operations per second. However, CPU-based LLM prompt processing for 7B models remains weak due to the absence of GPU acceleration. The hardware configuration makes this server suited for compute-focused applications such as software compilation, static web serving, CI/CD builds, and caching nodes.
